text.p: These are the leading stories in the Turkish press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Ruling Welfare Party members suprised by Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan's agreement to eight-year uninterrupted compulsory education which would lead to closure of the secondary level of religious schools.
- A Turkish general staff official says Erbakan is mistrusted, as he is seen trying to win time after a critical meeting with a top military-dominated council over the weekend.

- The former trade minister, who resigned on Saturday, says the Islamist-led government will collapse in a week with the help of other dissidents from the junior coalition partner, the True Path Party.
- Turkey establishes offices in seven provinces in an effort to register international suitcase trading, which is estimated to be worth over $13 billion annually.
- Thousands of people in shanty-towns within Istanbul live in poor conditions, experiencing bad health and poverty, with no effective support from the state.
- Infrastructure work on tourist areas between the coastal resorts of Ayvalik and Fethiye has not been completed ahead of the mass tourism season.
- The Black Sea Economic Cooperation forum meets in Istanbul to discuss projects in sectors such as energy, transportation, telecommunication and the environment.
- Syria may be able to halt a dam project in the southeast of Turkey for one and a half years if the United Nations votes in favour of a draft law on the usage of international waters.
